question: Who is the author of the book ‘Kitne Pakistan’, which won the Sahitya Akademi Award?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamleshwar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Kitne Pakistan’** is a critically acclaimed Hindi novel written by **Kamleshwar**, one of the most prominent writers in modern Hindi literature.
 
• The book was published in the year **2000** and earned widespread recognition for its unique narrative style and in-depth exploration of the historical and sociopolitical divisions in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• ‘Kitne Pakistan’ won the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **2003**, which is one of the highest literary honors in India, awarded by the Sahitya Akademi to recognize outstanding literary works in various Indian languages.
 
• The novel delves into themes of partition, religious intolerance, social justice, and the political and cultural history of the Indian subcontinent, making it a masterpiece in Hindi literature.
 
• Kamleshwar was a celebrated writer, screenwriter, and journalist who contributed immensely to Hindi literature and Indian cinema. His works often reflected deep socio-political concerns and human emotions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Kamleshwar:**

 
 
• **Kamleshwar** (1932–2007) was an eminent Hindi writer, screenwriter, and journalist who was a key figure in the modernist literary movement called **‘Nayi Kahani’** (New Story).
 
• He authored numerous novels, short stories, and essays, and was known for his bold and thought-provoking themes.
 
• Some of his other well-known works include **‘Raja Nirbansiya,’ ‘Kaali Aandhi,’** and **‘Pachpan Khambe Laal Deewarein’**.
 
• Kamleshwar also worked in the Indian film industry as a screenwriter and contributed to notable movies like **‘Aandhi,’ ‘Mausam,’** and **‘Chhoti Si Baat.’**
 
 
 
• **The Sahitya Akademi Award:**
 
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi Award** is a literary honor in India, established in **1954**, and presented annually by the Sahitya Akademi, India’s National Academy of Letters.
 
• This award recognizes outstanding literary works in **24 Indian languages**, including Hindi, English, and various regional languages.
 
• Winners receive a plaque and a cash prize, and the award is considered one of the most prestigious literary honors in India.
 
 
 
• **Theme of ‘Kitne Pakistan’:**
 
 
• The novel is a fictional courtroom drama where historical figures, events, and ideologies are brought together to debate the reasons and consequences of partition and communalism in South Asia.
 
• It critiques the political and social factors that led to the division of the Indian subcontinent and the subsequent violence and suffering.
 
• The narrative style is innovative, as it combines history, fiction, and philosophical inquiry to explore the human cost of division and intolerance.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Krishna Sobti:** Krishna Sobti was a renowned Hindi author and Sahitya Akademi Award winner, but she did not write ‘Kitne Pakistan.’ Her notable works include **‘Zindaginama’** and **‘Mitro Marjani.’**
 
• **Amrita Pritam:** Amrita Pritam was a celebrated Punjabi and Hindi writer, best known for her poem **‘Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu’** and novel **‘Pinjar.’** She did not author ‘Kitne Pakistan.’
 
• **Bhisham Sahni:** Bhisham Sahni, another stalwart of Hindi literature, is famous for his novel **‘Tamas,’** which deals with the partition of India. However, he was not the author of ‘Kitne Pakistan.’
